national.line: Ariana Grande wrote a kind note while watching the New York City Marathon, then surprised a runner named Ellie with it after she finished. Finish line, plus a pop star.
A 13-year-old contestant, Brianna Cameron, floored the coaches on The Voice Monday night with a sound compared to Whitney Houston. Those chairs never stood a chance.
Seventy years ago today, The Wizard of Oz aired on TV for the first time, and 53 percent of U.S. television viewers tuned in. Talk about a ratings yellow brick road.
A rescued stray gray kitten, just 7 weeks old, has the most perfect little goatee. Already looks ready for a board meeting.
Kelly Clarkson sang a ghoulish version of the Bee Gees' "Stayin' Alive" for Halloween, dressed as her favorite actress, Meryl Streep. Her Streep impression had range.
A clip shows Rowan Atkinson turning into Mr. Bean just by rolling his eyes, proof that acting can be that simple. One eye roll, whole new man.

pride.label: World Champion
pride.line: Victoria Moroski, 17, of Lake of the Ozarks won gold in the under-18 skim division at the World Wakesurf Championships in Hangzhou, China, in October, and Team USA won team gold. That's one way to make a splash.

pride.label: Student Project
pride.line: Waynesville Career Center welding and manufacturing students, led by instructor Adam Rodden, built backdrop props for the Waynesville High School Tiger Pride Marching Band, saving the band about $10,000. Now that's a metal band.

pride.label: School Record
pride.line: Fair Grove striker Jacob Shurtz broke the school record for goals in a season in October, passing his older brother Andrew's 31. Family dinner just got competitive.

pride.label: New Leader
pride.line: Lebanon R-3 Schools named Katie Cottongim its new Director of Communications. She'll have plenty to communicate.

local.line: Chick-fil-A opens its first Osage Beach location Thursday, Nov. 5, with a free entree for anyone who dresses in cow-themed attire. Cow costume, meet your biggest fan.

music.line: Carly Pearce, Jennifer Nettles and Carter Faith are on the soundtrack to Netflix's upcoming Heartland. Country is headed to streaming.
Zach Bryan covered "Kentucky Hurricane" by Kentucky songwriter Ian Noe and uploaded the video to YouTube. Nice way to share the spotlight.
Ty Myers is the first headliner announced for Musikfest 2027 in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania. Early bird gets the stage.
Shania Twain will kick off her 2027 UK tour in North Yorkshire. She's bringing the man, and the feelings, overseas.
Two brothers Irish step danced to Beyonce's country hit "Texas Hold 'Em" in a video that's pure delight. Country with a jig.
Miranda Lambert says writing "Over You" with ex-husband Blake Shelton was magical, calling it a very special song to both of them. Some songs outlast everything.

weird.line: Texas firefighters rescued a raccoon spotted high up in a tree with its head stuck in a hollow. Nobody asked how it got that curious.
A 60-year-old Pennsylvania man broke a Guinness World Record by attending 1,207 movie screenings in one year, about 3.3 a day. His popcorn budget must be wild.
Animal rescuers in Virginia solved the mystery of a hawk stuck in a driveway: the bird was too darn fat to fly. Somebody skipped leg day, and ate everything else.
A car stolen 30 years ago led to a surprise lien on a South Florida woman's license tag. Talk about a long-lost getaway car.
A black bear spotted on a school campus in Craryville triggered a lockout. The bear skipped the permission slip.
A rescued beaver named Blossom showed off his bowling skills, nudging a bright blue ball and mini-pumpkins around a Mississippi sanctuary. Strike one for the beavers.
A California officer was lifted to a hangar roof to save a baby raccoon and help reunite it with its mom. Best bucket ride ever.
A Wisconsin angler's 9.7-pound smallmouth bass from Green Bay broke a state record that had stood for about 75 years. That one did not get away.
A Hayward DNR team netted a record 7-foot-4 lake sturgeon in Sawyer County, Wisconsin. That's longer than most couches.
A U.S. student's jet-powered drone hit 491 mph, claiming the world's fastest-flight record for a drone. Don't try catching that with a net.
Honda is trying to break the world record with a 150-mph lawn mower. Saturday chores just got speedier.
Legend says that if you drive Route 351 near Koppel, Pennsylvania, at night, you might see a glowing green man. Check the headlights first.
A meteorite found in the Sahara turns out to be a 4.1-billion-year-old piece of Mars. Not bad for a rock that hitched a ride.
Scientists detected dinosaur blood cells in a 115-million-year-old fossil. Old blood, brand new headline.
A beaked dinosaur nicknamed the hell chicken is the first dinosaur discovered to eat fruit. Even dinosaurs wanted their five a day.
Scientists identified one of two 160-million-year-old squid fossils so fat they break every record. That squid never skipped dessert.
An island fox from California's Channel Islands is only about the size of a house cat. Smallest fox, biggest cuteness.
A friend's wedding gift went viral on Nov. 2 because it came presented with a packing slip. Gift receipt included, apparently.
A Florida man getting ready to sell his $500,000 home found a $10 quitclaim deed affecting his ownership stake. Ten bucks can complicate a lot.

humor.line: People are asked to use cliché phrases as much as possible, and the day's website lists 681 of them to choose from. It's not rocket science.
People are encouraged to hand a dollar to someone they know or a total stranger, and to tell them what day it is so they pass one along. Inflation's loss is a neighbor's gain.
It falls on the birthday of John Montagu, the Earl of Sandwich, born in 1718. Lunch with his name on it.
A jellyfish is about 95 percent water, and the lion's mane can weigh over 440 pounds. That's a lot of jelly for one toast.
It kicks off Eat Smart Month and began in 2017 with the American Heart Association. Good luck holding that line through Thanksgiving.
King Tut became pharaoh at age nine, and Howard Carter found his tomb in 1922. Today's nine-year-olds can barely run the TV remote.
Candy starts as sugar dissolved in water, and the hotter the water, the more sugar dissolves. Science has never tasted so good.
It honors Dr. Tina Dupree, who spent twelve years at one of the largest chicken restaurants in the world as Director of Community Relations and Training. Talk about a well-feathered career.
Kenner introduced the toy oven in 1963, and the original used an ordinary light bulb for heat. Cakes baked by lightbulb, that's a bright idea.
The old American Football League gave the game the scoreboard clock, two-point conversions and player names on jerseys. Finally, someone to blame for the two-point stress.
After Bank of America announced a $5 monthly debit card fee in 2011, credit unions reported 440,000 new customers in about five weeks. Five bucks can start a stampede.
The first American doughnuts were little nuts of dough the Pilgrims brought from Holland. Pilgrims were basically the first bakery.
Stephanie and Adrienne Vendetti of the website How to be a Redhead created it to help redheaded women love their hair. Ginger pride, officially.
Men who don't usually cook make dinner, while everyone who normally cooks stays out of the kitchen unless there's an emergency. A smoke alarm counts as an emergency.
James Naismith's first basketball game used peach baskets nailed ten feet high, a soccer ball and nine players per team. Nobody dunked yet.
Ballpark nachos started as "Margarita's State Fair Nachos," sold at the Dallas State Fair in 1964 by Sal Manriquez. Margarita deserves a seat at every game.
It falls on the birthday of its inventor, Adolphe Sax, born in Belgium in 1814. Elevator music owes him a thank-you.
Some people play it as a challenge, getting lost on purpose and finding their way back without a compass. Dad still won't ask for directions.
Florida attorney Nader Anise created it in 2001, and no lawyer jokes or lawyer bashing are allowed. Somebody tell the comedians.
The teddy bear was named after President Theodore Roosevelt after a 1902 cartoon showed him refusing to shoot a bear. Best thing a hunting trip ever produced.
In 1973, New Jersey became the first state to allow girls in Little League, a year after 11-year-old Marcia Pepe of Hoboken played three games for her team. A big win for fairness.
The word notary comes from nota, the shorthand Cicero's clerk Tiro used to take down Cicero's speeches. Fancy shorthand, serious stamp.
To count as dark chocolate it needs at least 35 percent cocoa solids, and chocolate-covered almonds are the classic pairing. Almonds make it practically health food.
Puns go back to Sumerian cuneiform and Egyptian and Mayan hieroglyphics, and today you're supposed to laugh instead of groan. Dad jokes are officially ancient.
Fans are told to read Dr. Seuss books like Fox in Socks and Oh Say Can You Say? out loud. Good luck on live radio.
Cappuccino is named for the hooded, reddish-brown robes of Capuchin friars, since cappuccio means hood in Italian. Your coffee is wearing a hood.
Pupusas are El Salvador's national dish, and cooking tools were found at Joya de Cerén, a site buried by volcanic ash about 2,000 years ago. Ancient lunch, still delicious.
The creators, Thomas and Ruth Roy, say don't forget the sauerkraut and garlic. Hope nobody has a date.
In Minsk, pianist Nikolai Panok once played for six hours without stopping to celebrate it. His fingers needed a vacation.
Early British puddings were savory and sometimes cooked in an animal stomach. Dessert has come a long way.
Carl Sagan's 1980 series Cosmos was the most widely viewed PBS program of its time. Science never looked so good on TV.
A fried chicken sandwich is handheld, so you can eat fried chicken and keep your hands clean. Napkins sold separately.
The Pennsylvania Dutch created scrapple, and one of its old names, pawnhaus, means finely chopped. Nothing goes to waste.
Greek yogurt is regular yogurt with the whey strained out, making it thicker and creamier. It's yogurt that hit the gym.
